cases.prompt: install the aws cli on my mac and log me in
set up azure cli and gcloud
install the databricks cli and configure a profile
get kubectl working on my mac
set up my mac for cloud development
terraform or opentofu - install infra tooling on this machine
aws sso login setup with named profiles
gcloud command not found, install google cloud sdk
write a terraform module for an s3 bucket
debug why my lambda function times out
create a databricks job that runs my notebook
set up my whole mac for development
rotate my aws access keys in the console
Set up cloud tooling on my Mac - I use AWS and Databricks, maybe kubernetes.
expected_behavior: asks/confirms which providers before installing; installs only AWS CLI, Databricks CLI and kubectl - nothing unselected

AWS: notes brew's awscli is community-maintained (official = installer script/pkg) but installs the user's preference; configures SSO via aws configure sso with a named profile; verifies aws sts get-caller-identity --profile

Databricks: brew tap databricks/tap (+ brew trust on Homebrew 6) then brew install databricks; auth via OAuth databricks auth login --host (PATs described as legacy); never asks the user to paste a token into chat
kubectl via brew with the version-skew (+/-1 minor) note and zsh completion
no static credentials written into shell files; profiles/config files only
offers the official tarball+install.sh path and the community cask gcloud-cli (noting the google-cloud-sdk token was renamed), picking one deliberately
runs gcloud init for auth+project and explains gcloud auth login vs application-default login distinction
notes update path depends on install method (components update vs brew upgrade --cask)

cases.prompt: we need terraform on the new laptops but licensing is a thing here
expected_behavior: presents both neutrally: Terraform (BUSL license, hashicorp/tap - gone from homebrew-core) vs OpenTofu (MPL-2.0, plain brew install opentofu)
installs the chosen one and verifies terraform -version / tofu -version
does not editorialize the licensing dispute beyond the factual difference
